missing_requirements.title: Token Revocation Propagation and Latency Boundary
missing_requirements.description: The system must define and enforce a strict upper bound on propagation latency for token revocation across all validation nodes to ensure revoked tokens are rejected immediately.
missing_requirements.justification: 1. When a token is revoked, distributed validation nodes evaluating incoming requests may cache validation results or lack synchronous updates; 2. Without a guaranteed synchronization bound or immediate check against a central revocation store, a compromised or logged-out token remains usable until cache expiration; 3. Therefore, a strict latency boundary or bypass check must be enforced to preserve the security guarantee of the revocation mechanism.

missing_requirements.title: Revocation State Store Failure Mode and Fail-Closed Guard
missing_requirements.description: The system must enforce a fail-closed policy if the token revocation state store becomes unavailable or experiences a timeout during token validation.
missing_requirements.justification: 1. State stores used for blacklisting or revocation checks can suffer network partitions, crashes, or timeouts; 2. If the system defaults to failing open (allowing tokens when the blacklist cannot be reached), an attacker could disrupt the state store to bypass revocation checks entirely; 3. Therefore, an explicit fail-closed guard is required to deny authentication when revocation state integrity cannot be verified.

missing_requirements.title: Revocation Store Storage Exhaustion and Pruning Policy
missing_requirements.description: The system must implement a retention and pruning policy for the token revocation state store to prevent unbounded growth and storage exhaustion.
missing_requirements.justification: 1. Every token revocation adds an entry to the state store that must typically persist at least until the token's natural expiration timestamp; 2. Storing expired token identifiers indefinitely leads to uncontrolled database size inflation and degradation of lookup performance; 3. Therefore, an automated pruning policy tied to token expiration timestamps is mandatory to ensure long-term data integrity and system stability.
